transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2025-12-15 15:00 PST | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions), Lina Gomez (EmberCare Head of IT), Rajiv Menon (EmberCare Security Architect), Sara Blake (Product), Tom Armitage (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery for EmberCare's evaluation of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus areas: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption and BYOK/KMS options, network/VPC topologies, and contractual SLAs around deletion/retention. Agreed next steps to share SOC2 and architecture diagrams and schedule a deeper infra session.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO)
- Identity (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC)
- Encryption (at-rest, in-flight, BYOK/KMS, HSM)
- Audit logs & retention policies
- Network/deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private VPC, on-prem)
- Contractual SLAs and data handling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood. How's it going?
[00:12] Lina Gomez: Good thanks, busy day. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:18] Marcus Patel: Hi all, Marcus on the SE side, I'll try to keep the deep infra stuff clear but I'm happy to jump in.
[00:28] Tom Armitage: Tom from procurement, I'll mostly listen for legal/contract points.
[00:35] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv, security. We had a couple documents from your site but want to walk through specifics around keys, logs, and SSO.
[00:47] Avery Chen: Totally, that's the plan. Quick run of agenda, and then dig into whichever you want. We're expecting questions around SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC granular roles, audit log retention, and keys - BYOK vs managed KMS, HSM options.
[01:05] Sara Blake: Also curious about differences in data residency and egress between Hosted and Dedicated, and what Private actually buys us beyond VPC.
[01:18] Marcus Patel: Good call. I'll start with a high-level, then we can jump in. So Redwood offers three deployment modes — hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra), and Private (VPC or on-prem with a customer-managed control plane). For security posture: our hosted offering runs on hardened infra with SOC2 controls, we provide encryption in transit and at rest by default. For customers requiring keys, we support BYOK via KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated in some configurations.
[01:46] Rajiv Menon: When you say HSM integrations — do you do Cloud HSM or do you recommend a customer HSM? Which providers?
[01:55] Marcus Patel: We support customer-managed keys through AWS KMS with CloudHSM backing on AWS, and equivalent key wrap options on GCP. For Private on-prem installs we can integrate with customer HSMs or HSM proxies, it's more of a deployment conversation. Small note: some of our docs call it 'BY-K' in shorthand, sorry if docs are terse.
[02:18] Lina Gomez: For SOC compliance, do you have a Type II report we can share with our auditors? And what about ISO?
[02:26] Avery Chen: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 certificate. We'll share the SOC2 report under NDA — I'll put that in the follow-up email.
[02:36] Tom Armitage: NDA ok, legal will review. On retention — we need 7 years for some logs and 90 days for user data, is that configurable?
[02:45] Marcus Patel: Audit logs and retention are configurable depending on deployment. Hosted customers can select retention tiers; we can push logs to a customer-owned S3 or logging endpoint for longer retention if needed. For Dedicated or Private, you control retention fully since logs can be forwarded to your logging stack.
[02:59] Rajiv Menon: How detailed are the audit logs — do they include token-level activity, prompt content, and system events?
[03:07] Marcus Patel: Good question. By default we log request metadata, timestamps, model version, route, and usage metrics. For customers needing deeper audit (e.g., request payloads or prompt-level metadata) we offer configurable audit capture, but that has privacy and retention trade-offs. We can also redact PII before forwarding.
[03:25] Lina Gomez: Is there a kill-switch or data deletion API? We need programmatic deletion within 48 hours for certain data classes.
[03:33] Avery Chen: We provide deletion APIs and retention controls. For Hosted, we document our deletion SLA; typical turnaround is 48–72 hours for complete purge across caches, KV, and backups unless the data is replicated to a customer target — then it depends on the destination. For Dedicated/Private, you generally control deletion. We'll include the exact contractual language in the SLA we send.
[03:56] Speaker 3: (mumbled) what about KV cash — I mean KV cache — are you clearing caches on deletion?
[04:04] Marcus Patel: Yes, KV cache purges are part of the deletion flow, but note there can be transient in-memory caches on long-running inference servers which we flush as part of the job. We should follow up with specifics for the model types you plan to use because long context sessions behave differently.
[04:24] Sara Blake: On identity, we use Okta, SAML, and SCIM for provisioning. We need SSO for both product console and API-level access, and SCIM sync for user lifecycle. How does Redwood handle that?
[04:36] Avery Chen: We support SAML SSO for the Console, and SCIM for provisioning. For API-level tokens we have RBAC and token scoping. You can tie API issuance to SSO or use a service principal model. We also support OIDC in some flows.
[04:51] Rajiv Menon: Can RBAC enforce least privilege by model and route? For example, product team can call hosted embeddings but not full generate?
[05:01] Marcus Patel: Yes, RBAC is route-aware. You can scope roles to specific endpoints/models and limit token permissions. For Dedicated/Private, we can add custom role mappings and integrate with your IdP for groups.
[05:12] Lina Gomez: Anything about provable audit trails for role changes? Our compliance requires logging of admin role changes and SSO events for 5 years.
[05:21] Marcus Patel: Admin role changes are captured in our audit logs and include actor, timestamp, and change details. For longer retention we recommend exporting logs to your SIEM. For Hosted customers we can forward logs; Dedicated/Private can natively write to your long-term storage.
[05:37] Tom Armitage: On encryption — do you encrypt embeddings at rest differently? We have concerns about exfil of highly sensitive embeddings for patient data.
[05:46] Marcus Patel: Embeddings are encrypted at rest using AES-256 and keys are managed via our KMS by default. For extra controls we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (BYOK). For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM so keys never leave your boundary. We can also do field-level encryption for highly sensitive payloads before they reach Redwood via client-side encryption libraries.
[06:10] Rajiv Menon: If we use hosted and BYOK, is there a way to rotate keys without downtime?
[06:17] Marcus Patel: Yes, rotation is supported; we use key versioning and key wrapping so existing data remains decryptable during rotation. There is an operational window but no full service outage for key rotation. We'll include the rotation playbook in the follow-up.
[06:31] Sara Blake: Network-wise, if we pick Dedicated, is it isolated in a VPC we control or a Redwood-managed VPC with peering?
[06:40] Marcus Patel: Dedicated is typically in a Redwood-managed VPC with network isolation per customer, and we support VPC peering or cross-account access patterns. For Private we can deploy into your VPC (VPC-integration) or on-prem. For the highest isolation we recommend Private with customer-managed control plane.
[06:57] Lina Gomez: For Private on-prem, what's involved in terms of support overhead and patching? We don't want to become the ops team for inference infra.
[07:08] Marcus Patel: Private on-prem comes with an install package and a support agreement. We do remote patch orchestration if you opt-in; alternatively we hand off the control plane and you operate. We usually propose a managed-private engagement where Redwood retains patching responsibility under an enterprise support contract.
[07:25] Avery Chen: Quick interjection — many customers start on Hosted to evaluate, then move to Dedicated or Private as compliance needs grow. That's a path we support with migration tooling.
[07:36] Rajiv Menon: About model updates: we need to control which model versions are allowed in prod. Is pinning supported?
[07:42] Marcus Patel: Yes, model version pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B) are supported. We have tracing hooks for rollbacks. We'll go over that in the technical deep-dive.
[07:53] Lina Gomez: Two other items — encryption in transit standards, and where are keys stored physically (region/residency)?
[08:01] Marcus Patel: We use TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit. Region residency for keys follows your KMS provider; if you use BYOK in a specific region, keys remain in that region. We'll attach a diagram showing region mapping.
[08:12] Speaker 2: (quiet) do you have any SOC2 controls around vendor management?
[08:18] Avery Chen: Yes, vendor management and third-party risk are covered in our SOC2 controls; we'll highlight the specific control IDs in the report.
[08:26] Tom Armitage: Contract language — do you offer data processing addendums (DPAs) and HIPAA BAAs? EmberCare handles PHI.
[08:36] Avery Chen: We offer DPAs by default and HIPAA BAA for customers processing PHI in supported deployment modes. For Hosted there are additional safeguards required to be HIPAA-ready; typically Dedicated or Private is recommended for PHI workloads. We'll have Legal follow up with sample BAA language.
[08:54] Rajiv Menon: Any wall-clock latency or perf differences if we encrypt client-side? Concern about CPU overhead for embeddings.
[09:03] Marcus Patel: Client-side encryption will add CPU and latency depending on payload size. For embeddings we typically recommend server-side envelope encryption plus network-level protection; if you need client-side, we'll measure in a pilot.
[09:18] Sara Blake: Are there restrictions on model families for Private? We run some tuned Llama variants internally — can we serve those?
[09:27] Marcus Patel: We onboard open models and many customer models; licensing matters for some model variants. For Private we can support custom models inside the deployment with a model onboarding checklist. We'll discuss runtime compatibility for quantized variants during the tech deep-dive.
[09:45] Avery Chen: Quick check — any competitors you're evaluating that we should be aware of?
[09:52] Lina Gomez: We're looking at Anthropic, Bedrock on AWS for an integrated approach, and a few smaller inference vendors for on-prem options. Also some teams trialing OpenAI endpoints for baseline.
[10:03] Marcus Patel: Good to know. We can highlight differences in control plane and BYOK options.
[10:10] Rajiv Menon: One more on logs — our compliance needs immutable logs for admin actions for 7 years. Can you attest to immutability?
[10:19] Marcus Patel: For immutability we recommend forwarding logs to a write-once S3 bucket with object lock enabled or to your SIEM. Redwood's internal logs are append-only per SOC2 controls, but long-term immutability is best handled in your custody.
[10:33] Lina Gomez: So next steps — we'd like the SOC2 and an infra diagram and then a deeper infra session with Marcus and our infra folks.
[10:43] Avery Chen: Sounds good. We'll send the SOC2 under NDA, attach an infra diagram showing Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and propose times for the week of 12/22 for the deep-dive. Marcus, you'll lead the infra session?
[10:55] Marcus Patel: Yep, I'll lead and prepare a Private VPC checklist and an example network playbook.
[11:02] Tom Armitage: Procurement will want a sample contract clause for deletion SLAs and BAA.
[11:09] Avery Chen: We'll loop in Legal for sample language.
[11:14] Rajiv Menon: One oddball: in your docs I saw 'KV cash' typo — can you confirm that's KV cache and whether cache tombstones are honored?
[11:24] Marcus Patel: Ha yes that's a typo we love. Cache tombstones on session termination are honored, but we need to review model specifics; we'll capture that in the tech doc.
[11:36] Sara Blake: That covers my list. Thanks.
[11:39] Avery Chen: Recap of immediate actions — Avery to send SOC2 + infra diagram, Marcus to prep Private VPC sketch and retention/playbook, and Rajiv to send any compliance redlines. We'll propose 3 times for next week.
[11:53] Lina Gomez: Great, talk soon.
[11:56] Meeting ends.
